correctness.rationale: Every allowed ordered window lies in a size-two orbit except f^2 self-invariant windows, giving the universal bound. If f=0 and t is odd, t^2 complement-paired cross-cut orbits would require an impossible odd signed flow across the P/N cut of a closed walk. The explicitly described edge types select all allowable orbits apart from the one necessary odd-case omission; the matched-block pattern cancels each internal edge imbalance and every neutral pattern balances vertexwise. Representatives are mutually bidirectionally connected, other moving vertices lie in directed cycles, and fixed symbols attach via length-two or length-three circuits. Thus Euler tours meet the respective upper bounds. Checker independently reconstructs 135 parameter graphs and verifies cyclic windows; four small exhaustive cases are supporting tests only.

originality.rationale: Mitchell--Wild arXiv:2603.25286 explicitly develops the modular-negation involution, proving the 1-fixed-symbol and 2-fixed-symbol special classes and posing arbitrary alphabet involutions as a further question. Their proven constructions cover those subcases and are acknowledged; they do not yield the exact odd-swap no-fixed-point parity deficiency or arbitrarily many fixed symbols. Primary reversed-window articles impose reversal rather than coordinatewise involution. The exact full span-two classification survived the performed semantic and literature comparisons; unindexed coverage remains possible.

value.rationale: The recent primary paper states the general alphabet-involution pair-selecting sequence question. Determining its complete sharp span-two solution for every involution orbit type, with a parity boundary where naive orbit counting fails and an explicit construction attaining that failure by exactly one, is a structural rather than a routine numerical contribution. The result forms a meaningful exact base case for the open higher-span problem.
